messages.author: ba89ff4c82e6597f
messages.subject: Re: Knitr PDF ok, but no content and error messages
parts: Ok guys, after getting some help on stackoverflow and playing around myself, I think I've found the solution....for any newbies like myself here's what you have to do, because knitr basically requires you to reproduce everything, you've done to get to your results and it allows you to work with relative paths, better than absolute paths.

\begin{document}
\title{My first Knitr Output File}
\author{Oliver M. Fisher, MD}
\maketitle{BMI Category Crosstabulation}

<<>>=
read.delim("~/relativepathtofile")
MIC1ELISANEW<-read.table("~/relativepathtofile", header=T)
@

<<>>=
attach(MIC1ELISANEW)
tab1=table(BMICat, Diagnosis)
tab1
summary(tab1)
@

<<>>=
tab1=table(MIC1ELISANEW$BMICat, MIC1ELISANEW$Diagnosis)
summary(tab1)
@

\end{document}

This'll get it to work.

Cheers,

O.

messages.subject: RE: [knitr] Re: Knitr PDF ok, but no content and error messages
parts:
Hi Ofish,

I wrote the Stack overflow answer.

Please note,

read.delim("~/relativepathtofile")

does not assign the results to anything (therefore is useless).

My suggestion of `read.table`, was to prompt you to read in the data (the same way you would read it into an new R session)

In
MIC1ELISANEW<-read.table("~/relativepathtofile", header=T)

replace read.table with the appropriate "read" function (delim / csv whatever you used originally), and replace 'relativepathtofile' with
the path to the file which contains the data (relative to the directory in which the .rnw script is stored).


Michael

Oliver

Is there a bizarre reason for that?

O.
